# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
uv workspace of four member packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |

Tracks: A — filing-index ingestion (known progression). There is one track because every
outcome feeds the same catalog.

## Open questions

1. The spec and the ADR are both PROPOSED (§7 step 1). Stages 1–4 do not depend on Azure. Stage 5
   needs the ADR to be accepted before it starts.
2. Package boundary: §4.9 places all of the code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The workspace
   also holds `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, and every one
   of them is an empty scaffold. Which package holds what is decided in Stage 1's brainstorming,
   unless you settle it first.
3. The root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` points to a module that does not exist. Keep it
   or drop it?
4. Stage 1 needs an SEC User-Agent identity (§4.8 `sec.user_agent`). It also needs one archived
   quarter and one already-published daily index for its live run (§7 step 4). The backfill range
   and the daily handoff date are needed only from Stage 2 on.

## Stages

The stages are ordered by dependency, not by outcome rank. Azure (O4, rank 4) comes after the
local stages, because every contract can be built and tested without it. The spec's §7 builds
the code and the infrastructure together in Phase 1; this roadmap diverges from that by putting
the infrastructure last.

- [ ] Stage 1: Core — one real quarter and one real daily index to Parquet
      Objective: Download one archived quarterly master index and one already-published daily master index, keep their original bytes, and parse both into canonical rows written as local Parquet.
      Outcomes: O1, O3 (at the smallest standard: one quarter, one daily file, run locally)
      Consumes: nothing (empty package scaffolds)
      Produces: a downloader that sends an identifying User-Agent and stays at or below 3 req/s; raw bytes stored with their SHA-256; a parser that yields `sec-index-v1` rows; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one real quarterly and one real daily `master.idx` are stored with byte count and SHA-256; O3 — both parse into Parquet with the §4.5 row contract, row counts recorded, and no malformed row is silently dropped; measured cost of the real run: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and observed request rate, all recorded in the findings file
      Leaves out: manifests and source state (Stage 2); the shared request budget (Stage 2); range backfill and daily discovery (Stage 2); generations and the active pointer (Stage 3); reconciliation (Stage 4); Azure (Stage 5); scheduling, alerts and the full validation suite (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Shared collector, source manifest and replay
      Objective: Provide the `discover`/`collect`/`transform` commands with durable source state, checkpointed backfill over a range, daily discovery with catch-up, one request budget, validated configuration and replay from raw storage.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5, O6, O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader, raw storage layout and parser
      Produces: source, snapshot, workset-binding, processing and attempt records (§4.5); immutable worksets; content-addressed raw and observation outputs; durable run reports; a single-issuer request-budget interface; typed configuration (§4.8); the §5 error outcomes for configuration, discovery, collection and access
      Exit: O1 — a backfill over a configured range reports complete, pending and failed units separately; O2 — daily discovery catches up across a missed run and a quarter boundary without advancing past a failed listing, and reports `no_new_sources`; O5 — backfill and daily ingestion use the same downloader and parser code paths; O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations from raw storage with zero SEC requests; O8 — concurrent collectors never exceed the single request budget, and retries count toward it; O11 — invalid configuration is refused before any network I/O
      Leaves out: generations and the active pointer (Stage 3); reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 4); the Storage-backed lease, Table Storage and ADLS (Stage 5); scheduling, alerts and Azure integration tests (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as an immutable generation, applying identity and precedence rules, behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O3, O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's observation outputs, processing records and run reports
      Produces: the `publish` command; generations with Parquet, `manifest.json` and `changes.parquet` (§4.5); a conditional-write pointer interface; the identity, deduplication and open-quarter precedence rules (§4.4)
      Exit: O3 — the canonical catalog for the Stage 1 quarter, plus daily overlap, holds no duplicate logical keys, and amendments stay distinct; O9 — injected crashes before the files finish, before the pointer update and just after it all leave readers seeing only complete generations, and a competing publisher cannot overwrite a newer pointer
      Leaves out: closed-quarter withdrawals and approvals (Stage 4); the Table Storage pointer backend (Stage 5); rollback runbooks (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Reconciliation and withdrawal approval
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources, publish additions and field updates, and hold closed-quarter key removals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 2's collector and Stage 3's publication path
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow; withdrawal-approval records; an `awaiting_approval` candidate state; change reports
      Exit: O7 — reconciling a changed quarterly snapshot records additions and updates, and unchanged hashes skip transformation; O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its exact source hash, open-quarter absence never withdraws a key, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key
      Leaves out: scheduled reconciliation and approval alerts (Stage 6); Azure deployment (Stage 5)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Azure deployment in an isolated environment
      Objective: Run the shared worker image on Container Apps Jobs, orchestrated by ADF, with ADLS, Table Storage and Log Analytics, in an isolated environment with every trigger disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 2–4's commands and their storage and pointer interfaces; an accepted ADR (Open question 1)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure as code under `infra/azure/sec-edgar-ingest/`; managed identities; a Storage-backed collector lease; Table Storage pointer and manifest backends; ADF pipelines with job start and poll
      Exit: O4 — in the isolated environment, fixture-based integration tests and fault injection pass (§6, Integration tests), and the bounded live smoke test plus a replay with SEC access disabled match §7 steps 3–5, with Azure cost recorded
      Leaves out: production schedules, alerts, runbooks and trigger enablement (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Scheduled operation and hardening
      Objective: Take the deployment through baseline backfill, daily catch-up and the first reconciliation to scheduled operation, with alerts, runbooks and the full validation suite.
      Outcomes: O2, O4, O7 (scheduled operation)
      Consumes: Stage 5's deployment and Stage 4's reconciliation
      Produces: ADF schedules; Azure Monitor alerts (§4.7); runbooks under `docs/runbooks/`; a release record; the complete §6 CI suite
      Exit: O2 — the daily trigger is enabled after catch-up is accepted, and scheduled runs are confirmed from their durable reports; O4 — production identities, alerts and rollback have been exercised, and the release record names the image and configuration versions and the active generations; O7 — the weekly reconciliation trigger is enabled after one manual run with any gated candidates resolved (§7 steps 6–9)
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and writing-plans copies it verbatim into the
stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick
> the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric (SKILL.md §6) over O1–O11. A row is met only on
path:line or test-name evidence, and its verdict names the stage plan that built it. A stamp
alone is not evidence. The spec's numbered requirements, R1–R11, are all cited in the `Spec`
column, so no uncited requirement is left to audit. Each unmet outcome exits one of two ways: as
a new stage, or as a conscious deferral with a written reason.
